name: TURKMENISTAN

flag.title: Flag of Turkmen.
flag.note: Green field, red gul stripe, crescent+stars

lead: Turkmenistan is a desert country in Central Asia. Karakum Desert sand covers 70% of it. Under the sand lies the world's 4th-largest store of natural gas. A burning pit called the Door to Hell draws adventurers.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Karakum means 'black sand' in Turkmen. This desert covers 70% of the country. Daytime heat hits 50°C. Hardy saxaul trees survive on barely a drop of rain.
The Caspian Sea lies to the west, and the Köýtendag mountains rise in the southeast. Turkmenistan borders Iran, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan.
animals: The Akhal-Teke is a horse breed 3,000 years old. Its coat shimmers like gold in sunlight. UNESCO (a UN culture group) lists its breeding tradition as living heritage.
Wild kulans (desert donkeys) roam the Karakum. Sand cats pounce on jerboas (tiny hopping rodents) at night. The endangered Persian leopard lives in the mountains.
culture: Turkmen carpets are family stories knotted in wool. Each clan has its own pattern, called a gul. Five carpet guls appear on the national flag.
Turkmen Horse Day, each April, is a holiday of parades and races for the Akhal-Teke. Plov, the national dish, is rice, meat, and carrots in one pot.
history: Ancient Turkmenistan sat on the Silk Road between China and Rome. The city of Merv, near today's Mary, held perhaps a million people in the 12th century.
Russia took the region in the 1880s. After independence in 1991, the first president renamed months after his family. He built a gold statue of himself that turned to face the sun.
wows: Ashgabat, the capital, holds a Guinness record: 543 buildings covered in white marble, the most anywhere.
Darvaza crater opened by accident in 1971, was lit to burn off gas, and burned for 50+ years.
Turkmenistan has the world's 4th-largest gas reserves.
Ashgabat banned non-white cars in 2018, as the president thinks white brings luck.
Hollow hairs make an Akhal-Teke shimmer like gold, with no dye.
Merv may have been the world's largest city in the 12th century.
In 1995, the UN recognised Turkmenistan's permanent neutrality (no sides in wars), the only such case.

myths.myth: Turkmenistan and Turkey are the same country
myths.fact: They are far apart, but their languages are cousins.

myths.myth: Nothing can grow in a desert country
myths.fact: The Karakum Canal carries river water across the sand. Farmers grow cotton and melons.
